title: Google is holding Gemini 4 Carbon for selected cyber defenders, Anthropic is showing companies what their Claude spend produced, Microsoft recorded $10 billion from OpenAI in one quarter, Google is taking ads in AI Mode to more countries, and Nvidia released an open model that transcribes recordings in 40 languages.
summary: On 28 October 2026 Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model it is giving first to a subset of cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, at the same introductory price as Argon. Anthropic made smart reports, in-app surveys and pooled group budgets generally available for Claude Enterprise. Microsoft’s Form 10-Q, filed the same day, recorded $10.0 billion of quarterly revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, and $7.2 billion still owed. On Alphabet’s earnings call, Google said it is expanding ads in AI Mode to international markets as Search ad growth slowed to 12%. Nvidia published Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open speech model for recordings of up to an hour.
uncertainty: Carbon’s scores and prices are Google’s, from its 28 October post. The three cybersecurity benchmarks were run without guardrails. Google does not give a date for general access, and the Fairwind page still describes Gemini 4 Argon, so the size of the Carbon group is not stated. Anthropic’s product page does not carry a date; TechCrunch reported the launch on 28 October. The cap of 10 reports a month, and the fact that reports stay off until an admin turns them on, are from Anthropic’s help center. Microsoft’s figures are from the Form 10-Q filed 28 October for the quarter ended 30 September. The filing does not split the $10.0 billion between cloud use and revenue-sharing, and it does not state a full-year OpenAI total. Azure’s $33,165 million and the 48% increase are in the same filing; the product table is in millions of dollars. The ad figures are TechCrunch’s account of Alphabet’s 28 October call. Nemotron’s error rates are Nvidia’s own leaderboard reading.

stories.theme: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon leads its cyber benchmarks, and only selected defenders can use it
stories.changed: On Wednesday 28 October 2026 Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its strongest model, built for cybersecurity and for long jobs that run on. Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google DeepMind’s chief AI architect, wrote the post. Google says Carbon ranks first on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, with a score of 59. On external tests run without guardrails, it reports 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities, 54.8% on ExploitGym for checking whether a flaw can be exploited, and 71.0% on Collinear’s CWE-bench for writing a fix. On Google’s own tests, Carbon more than doubles Argon’s success rate at writing secure code. Google says the Chrome team found Carbon more than 10 times better than another lab’s large frontier model at writing high-quality patches. It does not name that lab. Carbon also cut successful cheating on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to 0.0%, with cheat attempts at 0.4%, and high-severity misalignment alerts in Google’s own coding work fell by almost 80%. On Gray Swan’s indirect prompt-injection benchmark, Google says Argon’s attack success rate was 0.7% and Carbon’s is 0.0%. It reduced overreach by 26% and under-service by 29%, and it is fourth on WebDev Arena at 1768, up 89 elo. The introductory price matches Argon: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input at 95% off the input price. After the introductory period, the price is $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. Google does not say when that period ends. Access starts this week with a subset of cyber defenders, then more trusted partners in the Fairwind Program, while Google is in the US government’s voluntary pre-release testing. Developers, businesses and consumers are told to wait.
stories.matters: A model that finds flaws, tries exploits and writes patches is useful to a security team and useful to an attacker. Google is choosing who gets it, and the scores are the maker’s.
stories.imply: Do not put Carbon on a roadmap, a vendor comparison or a board slide until your team can actually call it. If someone quotes 88.2%, ask them to add that Google ran that test without guardrails.
uses: If you are a security team, ask whether you are in the Fairwind Program before you plan a pilot.
Keep your current review tools. Carbon is not a patch you can buy this week.
When a pitch cites Carbon’s benchmark lead, ask for the test, the guardrails, and who else has rerun it.
stories.example: A security lead is asked to switch the team’s coding assistant to Carbon because it ‘tops the chart’. She replies that the team is not on the defender list, that the 88.2% figure is Google’s and was run without guardrails, and that the pilot stays on the model they can call today.
stories.audience: Security leads, anyone buying coding agents, and people who brief leadership on model rankings.
stories.watch: When Google names a date for developers and for the API. Independent reruns of SEC-bench, ExploitGym and CWE-bench. Whether Fairwind’s terms for Carbon match the Argon rules already on that page.

source.title: Google: Introducing Gemini 4 Carbon, 28 October 2026
source.quote: Starting this week, we will make Carbon available to a subset of cyber defenders and will gradually phase access to additional trusted partners through our Fairwind Program.

stories.theme: Anthropic will show a Claude Enterprise team what it produced, what it cost, and where the work stalled
stories.changed: On Wednesday 28 October 2026, TechCrunch reported that Anthropic had made a new set of Claude Enterprise controls generally available. Anthropic’s own page describes three of them. Smart reports: an admin picks a team, a date range and the products to include, and Claude reads a sample of that team’s transcripts, groups the work into workstreams, and shows the spend, the deliverables and the common friction, such as a missing connector or a failed tool call. Each report ends with one list of recommendations, including workflows to turn into skills. Findings can be shared as an artifact. Owners can let a team lead who is not an admin run a report for their own group. The page says the reports are for understanding adoption and planning spend, and that they are not for evaluating individual performance or making employment decisions. In-app surveys ask people, in the tool they are already using, what Claude changed about the time a task took and what would break if access went away. Survey answers are treated as the customer’s data. Pooled group budgets give a group one shared monthly budget, with each person’s own limit still in place. Every request counts against both, and the person stops at whichever runs out first. Admins with billing permission get email at 50%, 75%, 95% and 100% of a budget. Availability depends on configuration, including organisations that use a HIPAA setup or customer-managed encryption keys. Anthropic’s help center, updated with the launch, says reports are off until an admin turns them on, and that each organisation can run up to 10 reports a month at no charge. A queued or in-progress report counts; a failed one does not.
stories.matters: Leaders have been asked what the AI bill bought. This is Anthropic’s answer for its own product: a sample of the transcripts, a cost, and a warning not to turn it into a score for a person.
stories.imply: Turn the report on for one team and read the friction list. Keep performance reviews on the work itself. A sample of transcripts is not the whole month.
uses: Run one report for a team whose Claude bill you already question, and read the workstreams beside the spend.
Write down that the report is not an input to a performance review, and say so when you share it.
If you use customer-managed keys, a HIPAA configuration, or want Claude Code included under zero data retention, check the help center before you promise the board a report.
stories.example: An engineering director runs the one free report she needs this month on the platform team. It shows a workstream stuck on a missing connector. She sends that finding to the admin who owns connectors, and she leaves the report out of the promotion packet.
stories.audience: Claude Enterprise admins, finance partners who see the token bill, and the managers who will be handed the report.
stories.watch: Whether the 10-report cap changes. Whether OpenAI and Google ship a report a manager can share without it becoming a score. How customers with encryption keys are told they are left out.

source.title: Anthropic: Smart reports, surveys, and pooled group budgets for Claude Enterprise
source.quote: Smart reports help admins understand adoption and inform investment planning, but they aren’t for evaluating individual performance or making employment decisions.

stories.theme: Microsoft recorded $10 billion from OpenAI in the September quarter, and $7.2 billion is still owed
stories.changed: On Wednesday 28 October 2026 Microsoft filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. The filing says Microsoft holds an equity-method investment in OpenAI of an approximate 24% interest on an as-converted basis, and that OpenAI is a related party. For the three months ended 30 September 2026, Microsoft recorded revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, inclusive of revenue-sharing payments, of $10.0 billion. Accounts receivable from OpenAI were $7.2 billion at 30 September, and $6.0 billion at 30 June. Microsoft has made funding commitments of $13.0 billion, of which $12.0 billion was funded as of 30 September. The same filing’s product table, which is in millions of dollars, lists Azure revenue at $33,165 million for the quarter, against $22,384 million a year earlier, and total revenue at $92,279 million. In the narrative, Microsoft says Azure revenue increased 48%. The filing does not say how much of the $10.0 billion was cloud computing and how much was revenue sharing.
stories.matters: A large slice of a cloud giant’s quarter is one AI lab that also owes it $7.2 billion. That is demand, and it is concentration.
stories.imply: When a forecast treats Azure growth as broad enterprise demand, ask how much of the quarter was OpenAI. The filing gives you the OpenAI line. It does not give you the split inside it.
uses: If you buy from both, note that your cloud bill and their revenue-sharing sit in the same disclosed total.
In a board note on cloud growth, separate the OpenAI line from the rest of Azure. The 10-Q now lets you do that for the total, not for the mix.
Treat the $7.2 billion receivable as money not yet collected, which is what the filing says it is.
stories.example: A treasurer updating the cloud forecast writes two lines: OpenAI arrangements, $10.0 billion of Microsoft revenue this quarter, and OpenAI receivables, $7.2 billion. She leaves the cloud-versus-sharing split blank because the filing does.
stories.audience: Finance teams, investors, and anyone reading Azure’s growth as a signal of wider AI demand.
stories.watch: Whether the next 10-Q splits cloud revenue from revenue sharing. Whether the receivable rises or gets collected. Any change to the approximate 24% stake.

source.title: Microsoft Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, filed 28 October 2026
source.quote: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, inclusive of revenue-sharing payments, of $10.0 billion.

stories.theme: Google is putting ads in AI Mode outside the United States as Search ad growth slows
stories.changed: On Wednesday 28 October 2026, during Alphabet’s quarterly earnings call, Google said it is expanding ads in AI Mode beyond the United States. TechCrunch reported the call. Philipp Schindler, Google’s chief business officer, said the company is scaling ads within AI Overviews in AI Mode to more users and queries, taking that monetisation global for the first time, and that it is also adding multi-turn ads in AI Mode in the US. He said click-through rates for sponsored product listings in AI Mode are already comparable to those for organic listings, and that user research finds the ads relevant. TechCrunch reports Alphabet revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% from a year earlier, and that the shares fell 8% after the results. Google Search revenue grew 12% in the third quarter, after 17% in the second quarter and 19% in the first. Sundar Pichai said Search queries grew at their fastest year-over-year rate in five years, without giving the rate. He said queries in AI Mode are three times longer on average than traditional searches, and that one in five AI Mode searches globally involves voice, images or documents. Google has also passed 50 billion visual searches a month. Google Services revenue was $96.3 billion, up 11%. Google Cloud revenue was $30.7 billion, up 103%.
stories.matters: The answer box is becoming an ad slot in more countries. If you buy search ads, or you depend on the free listing above them, the place your customer looks has changed.
stories.imply: Check whether your ads are eligible for AI Mode in each country you sell in. A longer query is a different keyword plan. ‘Comparable’ click-through is Google’s description, not a rate you can put in a forecast.
uses: Ask your search team which countries just gained ads inside AI Mode, and which campaigns are opted in.
Pull a week of AI Mode queries before you rewrite keywords. Pichai says they are three times longer on average.
If you live on organic traffic, look at whether a sponsored listing now sits in the AI answer for your product terms.
stories.example: A retail media lead adds AI Mode placements to the UK and Germany accounts, keeps the US multi-turn ads in a separate line, and tells finance she will not book a click-through rate until she has her own numbers.
stories.audience: Search and media buyers, ecommerce teams, and anyone whose pipeline starts with a Google query.
stories.watch: Which countries are actually live. Whether Google publishes a click-through rate rather than ‘comparable’. How organic results move once the ad is inside the answer.

source.title: TechCrunch: Google expands AI Search ads globally as core ad growth slows, 28 October 2026
source.quote: Today, we’re announcing the expansion of ads in AI mode into international markets alongside multi-turn ads and AI mode in the U.S.

stories.theme: Nvidia’s open Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe turns a recording into a transcript, with speakers, in 40 languages
stories.changed: On Wednesday 28 October 2026 Nvidia published Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a speech model it is releasing under the OpenMDW-1.1 licence, with a fine-tuning toolkit in NeMo Speech. One model does verbatim or cleaned-up transcripts, speaker labels, translation, spoken language identification in 40 languages, and word-level timestamps, on recordings of up to one hour. The style is chosen with a written instruction for that request, without retraining. Nvidia says it has about 4.3 billion active parameters. It reports a mean word error rate of 4.71% on the nine public test sets of the English Open ASR Leaderboard and 4.62% on the multilingual Open ASR Leaderboard, and calls that the best open-weights result on those boards. Given a list of expected names, it says named-entity errors on ContextASR-Bench fall six-fold. With its NVFP4 checkpoint and a DFlash2 draft model, served by the Nemotron Transcribe NIM, it says the model transcribes up to 2,238 seconds of audio per second on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU. Nvidia also says that on 17 tasks the model can be adapted on a single GPU, typically within 0.5 to 2.3 GPU-hours per task. Checkpoints include BF16, FP8, NVFP4, GGUF and a DFlash2 draft.
stories.matters: Meeting notes and call transcripts are a daily job. An open model you can prompt, and run where you choose, is a different offer from a closed transcription API.
stories.imply: Try it on a recording you already have a human transcript for. The error rates are Nvidia’s. A one-hour recording is the length it states. Judge the names, the speakers and the language you actually use.
uses: Transcribe one real meeting, with a prompt that says whether you want every false start or a cleaned paragraph, and compare it with the notes you trust.
If the recording has product names, pass them in the prompt. Nvidia’s six-fold claim is for that setup, on its benchmark.
Keep live call-centre audio on the system you have until you have tested this model on recordings of that length and accent.
stories.example: An operations lead runs last Tuesday’s customer call through Nemotron, asks for speaker labels and a cleaned transcript, and checks the account names against the CRM before anyone files the note.
stories.audience: Teams that transcribe meetings, support calls or research interviews, and the IT group that decides where audio is allowed to go.
stories.watch: Independent word-error rates, especially outside English. Whether a local build on ordinary hardware matches the Blackwell figure. How the OpenMDW licence treats a commercial deployment.

source.title: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, published 28 October 2026
source.quote: The transcription style is chosen with a natural language instruction for each request, without retraining.
